content:
After a long period of developer and public beta testing, Apple has officially rolled out macOS 26.6 to all supported Mac users. Here's what's included in this update.

macOS 26.6 officially arrives

macOS 26.6 has been released, fixing over 150 security vulnerabilities and containing other bug fixes and performance improvements. These include issues where some Intel-only applications incorrectly displayed deprecation notices, bugs related to HealthKit, and issues with HDR screenshots in Messages.

For users planning to upgrade to macOS 27 "Golden Gate" later this year, macOS 26.6 will begin pre-indexing for the new Siri AI, the new Siri application, and features related to the next generation of Apple Intelligence.

Apple has only confirmed that this process will occur for iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, but it appears that the Mac side will follow the same approach. As users currently running the macOS 27 beta are aware, the indexing process can take several days, so starting early should help reduce waiting time after upgrading later.

The official build number for macOS 26.6 is 25G72, which differs from the release candidate (25G70) issued last week.

Have you discovered anything new in macOS 26.6? Let us know in the comments.
